status: Third retrospective exploratory extension, after viewing the static and rolling audits
question: Does a shared monthly-weather response transfer better after removing source-city or source-period concentration scales, with fewer target sentinel cities?
source_features: Only monthly aviation weather and hemisphere-aligned seasonal terms; no annual POWER, EDGAR, absolute location, target lags or target-country labels
source_labels: standardized source-country calendar-month spatial log contrast
source_training_eligibility: Observed monthly temperature, humidity, wind; temperature in [-80,60] C, humidity in [0,100] percent, wind in [0,80] m/s
target_eligibility: Same weather-quality condition, applied before learned gates; denominator remains all target FUA-months
sentinel_design: Nested subsets of the ten fixed development cities; other-city audit remains disjoint from all ten development cities
target_fit: Log-scale affine Ridge calibrated on strictly earlier sentinel labels, with empirical retransformation smearing; no current audit labels
gate_complexity: Mandatory observed-weather eligibility plus no more than two learned inequalities
gate_thresholds: Discovery covariate quantiles [0.1,0.25,0.5,0.75,0.9]; top 12 single conditions supply two-condition candidates
discovery_success: At least 5 percent improvement over the best same-fit-budget target-only baseline on identical accepted observations, positive in both discovery years
replication_success: Discovery success, 5 percent improvement, positive paired cluster-bootstrap lower bound, at least 25 percent row and FUA coverage, at least 5 FUAs and 12 months, at both later stages
budget_accounting: Report sentinel_count * window per update, cumulative unique fitted labels, and 240 development labels separately; discovery labels are not free
inference: Prediction-oriented observational conditions; no causal identification or new untouched-data claim
input_target: Existing SatPM FUA-month means, not regulatory observations
